dossier.purpose: Next.js (npm package `next`, 16.3.8, MIT) is a React web-application framework: the `next` CLI (dev/build/start), a Node.js HTTP server runtime (App Router and Pages Router, RSC rendering, ISR/caching, image optimizer) and a Rust toolchain (Turbopack + SWC, shipped as a native N-API addon with a wasm fallback), kept in one monorepo with docs (456 .mdx files) and about 224 example apps. It is an application framework, not container tooling: this repo contains no tool that defines or runs a multi-service application (app plus services, volumes, networks) on a container engine. Its docs name 'Docker container' as a deployment target, and four examples (examples/with-docker, with-docker-compose, with-docker-multi-env, with-docker-export-output) supply Dockerfiles and Compose files that are run with the external `docker compose` CLI (examples/with-docker-compose/README.md:44-52,68-74; examples/with-docker/README.md:21-43). The only container-aware product code is Docker detection via the vendored is-docker module.

claims.claim: [README] 'Next.js enables you to create full-stack web applications by extending the latest React features, and integrating powerful Rust-based JavaScript tooling for the fastest builds.'

[README] The README has no install command, no container/Docker/Compose/deployment/hosting statement, no platform list and no telemetry statement. It only links to nextjs.org/docs, Learn, Showcase, Discussions, Discord and contributing.md.
[README] Security: 'we encourage you to responsibly disclose this and NOT open a public issue'; bug-bounty reports go by email to responsible.disclosure@vercel.com.
[README] License badge links to license.md; the file is the MIT License, Copyright (c) 2025 Vercel, Inc.

[docs] 'Next.js can be deployed as a Node.js server, Docker container, static export, or adapted to run on different platforms.' Feature support: Node.js server All, Docker container All, static export Limited, adapters Varies.

[docs] 'Docker deployments support all Next.js features'; Next.js 'can be deployed to any provider that supports Docker containers ... container orchestrators like Kubernetes'; per-feature tables also list 'Docker container: Yes'.

[docs] Prefer local development (npm run dev) over Docker on Mac/Windows during development: host-to-VM file sharing can delay Fast Refresh by seconds to minutes; reserve Docker for production and production-build testing.
[docs] By default the cache lives in memory (50 MB) and on the local disk of each instance; under Kubernetes 'each pod will have a copy of the cache'; use cacheHandler/cacheHandlers to share it.

[docs] Multi-instance deployments must share NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY (base64 AES key); the same build should boot multiple containers (use generateBuildId); set deploymentId for version-skew protection.

[docs] 'This allows you to use a singular Docker image that can be promoted through multiple environments with different values' (server-side env read at request time; NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are inlined at build time).
[docs] A reverse proxy such as nginx is recommended in front of the Next.js server; the only platform requirement is 'a Node.js server' (plus the sharp package for Image Optimization).

[example README] with-docker-compose: 'Run multiple Next.js apps, databases, and other microservices in a single deployment'; multistage + output standalone gives ~110 MB vs ~1 GB; develop locally without Node.js or TypeScript installed.

[example README] with-docker: compose.yml offers a Node.js and a Bun service ('Run one service at a time to avoid port conflicts'); non-root user, BuildKit cache mounts, standalone output; deployable to Cloud Run, ECS/Fargate, Azure Container Instances, DigitalOcean App Platform or any Kubernetes cluster.

install.method: create-next-app via npx (docs; requires Node.js >=20.9; OS-agnostic incl. Linux/macOS/WSL)
Manual install into an existing project (npm)
Scaffold and run the Docker Compose example (requires Docker with Compose; this installs an example app, not Next.js itself)
install.command: npx create-next-app --example with-docker-compose with-docker-compose-app; docker network create my_network; docker compose -f compose.prod.yaml build; docker compose -f compose.prod.yaml up -d

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - docs list Linux as a supported OS (docs/01-app/01-getting-started/01-installation.mdx:51); native N-API binaries are built for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and -musl (.github/workflows/build_and_deploy.yml:231-240) and published as @next/swc-linux-x64-gnu / -musl (crates/next-napi-bindings/npm/linux-x64-gnu/package.json:9-17). Cargo unit tests run on x86-64 Linux (.github/workflows/build_and_test.yml:288-296); most JS e2e jobs run on ARM Linux runners (build_and_test.yml:443).
platforms.wsl2: yes (documented; no dedicated CI job found) - docs: 'Operating systems: macOS, Windows (including WSL), and Linux' (docs/01-app/01-getting-started/01-installation.mdx:51); WSL 2 is recommended with the project inside the VM filesystem, not /mnt/c (docs/01-app/02-guides/local-development.mdx:71-77). Code only detects WSL for telemetry (packages/next/src/telemetry/anonymous-meta.ts:3,47); CI has Windows jobs (build_and_test.yml:940-1021) but no WSL job.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes - docs list macOS (installation.mdx:51); aarch64-apple-darwin native binary is built on macos-15 (build_and_deploy.yml:219-222) and published as @next/swc-darwin-arm64 (crates/next-napi-bindings/npm/darwin-arm64/package.json:9-14); the CLI warns when x64 Node runs under Rosetta on Apple Silicon (packages/next/src/bin/next.ts:115-125). No macOS test job found: 'macos' appears in workflows only at build_and_deploy.yml:37,219 and build_reusable.yml:308-309.
platforms.gpu: no - not applicable; grep for cuda/gpu/nvidia in packages/next/src (excluding compiled) and in docs/ returned zero matches.

integrations.cli: yes - `next` bin (packages/next/package.json:80-82; packages/next/src/bin/next.ts): build, dev (default), start, info, telemetry, typegen, upgrade, experimental-analyze, experimental-test, experimental-request-insights and internal {trace, query-trace, post-build, upload-trace, static-routes-info} (bin/next.ts:178-799). Also `create-next-app` (packages/create-next-app/package.json:17-19). No container or compose subcommand exists.
integrations.mcp: Built-in MCP server (Streamable HTTP) at /_next/mcp, mounted only in the dev server and enabled by default (experimental.mcpServer: true - packages/next/src/server/config-shared.ts:2250; mounted at server/dev/hot-reloader-turbopack.ts:1171-1173 and hot-reloader-webpack.ts:1686-1701; route check server/mcp/get-mcp-middleware.ts:18; no auth check in :11-46). Code registers 9 tools (get_project_metadata, get_errors, get_page_metadata, get_logs, get_server_action_by_id, get_routes, get_request_insights, get_compilation_issues and compile_route - the last two Turbopack-only) at server/mcp/get-or-create-mcp-server.ts:44-75; docs list 8 and omit get_request_insights (docs/01-app/02-guides/mcp.mdx:81-88). The separate npm package `next-devtools-mcp` (not in this repo) is the documented client bridge (mcp.mdx:9,15-30). No MCP endpoint on the production server path found.
integrations.sdk_or_api: Library API of npm package `next`: programmatic server `import next from 'next'; next({dev}).getRequestHandler()` (docs/01-app/02-guides/custom-server.mdx:18-38; packages/next/src/server/next.ts); Deployment Adapter API `NextAdapter` with modifyConfig/onBuildComplete (docs/01-app/03-api-reference/07-adapters/02-creating-an-adapter.mdx:38-68; adapterPath hook packages/next/src/build/index.ts:4461-4481; NEXT_ADAPTER_PATH at server/config-shared.ts:2157); custom cache handlers cacheHandler/cacheHandlers (docs self-hosting.mdx:111-125). No hosted vendor HTTP API; the HTTP surface is the served app plus built-in /_next/image (server/next-server.ts:942) and dev-only /_next/mcp.
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: Claude Code plugin marketplace manifest .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (plugin 'nextjs', source ./skills) and plugin manifest skills/.claude-plugin/plugin.json; 4 skills in skills/ (next-dev-loop, next-cache-components-adoption, next-cache-components-optimizer, next-partial-prefetching-adoption); documented skill install `npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-dev-loop` (docs/01-app/02-guides/ai-agents.mdx:172). create-next-app generates AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (ai-agents.mdx:37), and `next dev` writes or updates them when it detects an AI coding agent unless `agentRules: false` (packages/next/src/server/lib/start-server.ts:511-534; server/lib/generate-agent-files.ts:90-123). Docs say Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot read AGENTS.md (ai-agents.mdx:33); version-matched docs ship inside the package at dist/docs (packages/next/taskfile.js:36-45). No Codex-specific plugin found.

readme.telemetry_and_network: README is silent on telemetry. Docs: 'completely anonymous' telemetry, opt-out with `next telemetry disable` (docs/01-app/03-api-reference/06-cli/next.mdx:161-173). Code: on by default; disabled when env NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED is any non-empty string (including '0') or via the conf flag (packages/next/src/telemetry/storage.ts:135-154). Events are POSTed to https://telemetry.nextjs.org/api/v1/record (telemetry/post-telemetry-payload.ts:25; 5 s timeout, 1 retry, errors swallowed). Payload: random anonymousId and salt kept in a `conf` store, sessionId, projectId = SHA-256(salt + `git config --local --get remote.origin.url` | REPOSITORY_URL | cwd) (storage.ts:156-172; project-id.ts:43-47), plus platform, OS release, arch, CPU count/model/speed, memory, isDocker, isWsl, isCI/ciName, nextVersion and detected AI-agent name (anonymous-meta.ts:8-23). In CI/Docker the conf is stored under <distDir>/cache (storage.ts:41-49). Telemetry objects are created on next build, next dev, export/analyze (build/index.ts:1208; cli/next-dev.ts:150; server/lib/router-server.ts:159-166 gated on opts.dev); no construction on the production-server path was found. NEXT_TELEMETRY_DEBUG prints events to stderr instead of sending (storage.ts:292-310). Example Dockerfiles leave `NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` commented out (examples/with-docker/Dockerfile:49-52,84-87). Other network use: `next dev` fetches https://registry.npmjs.org/-/package/next/dist-tags for a staleness notice (server/dev/hot-reloader-shared-utils.ts:17; errors ignored); if the platform SWC package is missing, it downloads @next/swc-* from the configured npm registry and may fall back to wasm (build/swc/index.ts:262-293,308-383; lib/download-swc.ts:37-41; opt out of wasm fallback with NEXT_DISABLE_SWC_WASM, index.ts:235); next/font/google fetches CSS from fonts.googleapis.com and font files at build/dev, honours http(s)_proxy, and can be mocked via NEXT_FONT_GOOGLE_MOCKED_RESPONSES (packages/font/src/google/get-google-fonts-url.ts:50; fetch-resource.ts:10-57; get-proxy-agent.ts:10-20; fetch-css-from-google-fonts.ts:17-18); create-next-app runs an update check at startup with no opt-out found (packages/create-next-app/index.ts:778-780) and downloads examples from api.github.com/codeload.github.com when --example is used (create-next-app/helpers/examples.ts:41-139). Opt-in only: `--experimental-upload-trace <url>` (bin/next.ts:217-219,373-375) and `next internal upload-trace` to https://nextjs.org/api/upload-trace (cli/internal/upload-trace.ts:4). Accounts: none needed to build, run or self-host; Vercel credentials are used only by the repo's own deploy tests and benchmarks (contributing/core/testing.md:139-150; bench/vercel/README.md:5-11).

Rust - crates/ (221 .rs files) and turbopack/ (785 .rs files); nightly toolchain pinned (rust-toolchain.toml:4)

entry_points.what: `next` CLI (commander): build, dev (default), start, info, telemetry, typegen, upgrade, experimental-*, internal; published as bin ./dist/bin/next (packages/next/package.json:80-82)
HTTP server main shared by next dev, next start and standalone server.js; handles SIGINT/SIGTERM graceful shutdown (:399-480)
Lines 1418-1467 generate .next/standalone/server.js (reads PORT default 3000, HOSTNAME default 0.0.0.0, KEEP_ALIVE_TIMEOUT; calls startServer)
Programmatic API next({dev}) used by custom servers
Rust N-API addon (next-swc.*.node) loaded by packages/next/src/build/swc/index.ts; wasm fallback built from crates/wasm

code.architecture: Monorepo (pnpm workspaces + Turborepo + Lerna; 19 package.json under packages/). packages/next/src: bin/ + cli/ (commander CLI); build/ (build orchestration index.ts, webpack-config.ts, turbopack-build/, swc/ loader of native or wasm bindings, adapter/ hook, utils.ts standalone tracing); server/ (next.ts public API, next-server.ts, base-server.ts, lib/router-server.ts, lib/start-server.ts, app-render/ RSC rendering, dev/ HMR dev server, lib/incremental-cache/ file-system + custom cache handlers, use-cache/, image-optimizer.ts, mcp/); client/ and shared/ (browser runtime and router); telemetry/ and trace/; compiled/ (vendored, ncc-precompiled dependencies with 153 LICENSE files in the tree). Rust: crates/next-napi-bindings (N-API addon), next-api, next-core, next-custom-transforms (SWC transforms), wasm; turbopack/crates/* (~53 crates: turbo-tasks, turbopack-core, -ecmascript, -css, -node, ...). Other packages: create-next-app, eslint-config-next, eslint-plugin-next, font, next-codemod, next-env (.env loading: .env.<mode>.local, .env.local, .env.<mode>, .env), next-mdx, next-routing, next-swc, third-parties, next-rspack. Also docs/ (bundled into the package as dist/docs), examples/, test/, bench/, evals/, skills/ (Claude Code plugin), scripts/. Container material is limited to examples/with-docker*, .devcontainer/devcontainer.json (single contributor image plus features), scripts/native-builder.Dockerfile (release builder) and a Playwright container in test_examples.yml; none define a multi-service app.
code.packaging_and_release: Artifacts are npm packages: `pnpm publish --recursive` of ./packages/** (next, create-next-app, @next/* ...) plus eight per-platform native packages @next/swc-{darwin-arm64,darwin-x64,linux-arm64-gnu,linux-arm64-musl,linux-x64-gnu,linux-x64-musl,win32-arm64-msvc,win32-x64-msvc} (crates/next-napi-bindings/npm/*; scripts/publish-release.js:105-151) and wasm packages @next/swc-wasm-web/-nodejs (publish-release.js:153-187; built at .github/workflows/build_and_deploy.yml:496-556). At publish time `next` gains the native packages as optionalDependencies and devDependencies/scripts are stripped (publish-release.js:208-229); `next` has no install lifecycle scripts (packages/next/package.json:83-93). Flow: trigger_release.yml (daily cron + manual dispatch) -> scripts/start-release.js -> push of tag v* -> build_and_deploy.yml builds binaries on macos-15, Windows and Ubuntu (docker builder image scripts/native-builder.Dockerfile, build_and_deploy.yml:197-241,383-421) -> publishRelease job in a per-channel GitHub Environment with id-token: write (:619-686) runs publish-release.js. The workflow uploads only workflow artifacts (:483-487); GitHub releases are un-drafted for prereleases (publish-release.js:251-313). Integrity: root .npmrc:4 sets `provenance = true` and actions are SHA-pinned (build_and_deploy.yml:55), but publish-release.js passes no --provenance flag (the only explicit --provenance is release-next-rspack.yml:123,130) and no checksum, cosign/sigstore or GPG signing steps exist for the .node binaries (grep of .github/workflows and scripts). Whether published tarballs carry attestations cannot be verified from source. No Docker image is built or published by this repo for Next.js apps.
code.tests_and_ci: Frameworks: Jest 29.7 + Playwright 1.61 driven by `node run-tests.js` / scripts/run-jest.sh (package.json:54-58,224,250); e2e/development/production suites create isolated installs in a temp dir and start a server on a random port (contributing/core/testing.md:36-42); Rust via cargo nextest (.config/nextest.toml; packages/next-swc/package.json:22) plus doc tests; lint via ESLint 9, Prettier, tsc 6.0.2, ast-grep rules (.config/ast-grep/rules) and alex. Approx. test files (*.test.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}): 1,903 under test/ (e2e 1,136; production 358; development 298; unit 110) and 194 under packages/; Rust sources are in 221 (crates/) + 785 (turbopack/) .rs files, not separately counted. CI: 36 workflow files. build_and_test.yml (PR + push to next-16-3) runs build-native/build-next, lint (pnpm lint-no-typescript, check-examples, validate-externals-doc), types-and-precompiled, cargo unit tests (x86-64) / rust-check / rustdoc, unit tests on Node 20 and 22 (Linux and Windows), webpack dev/prod e2e sharded 10 ways x React default and 18.3.1 on Linux ARM runners, Turbopack dev/prod (7 shards), Rspack (label-gated), cache-components suites, wasm SWC test, Firefox/WebKit, new-test flake detection, deploy tests against Vercel preview builds; merge is gated by the aggregate `tests-pass` job (build_and_test.yml:1182-1225). test_examples.yml runs `run-tests.js --type examples` every 4 h in a Playwright Docker container (:11-12,56). Nothing builds or runs the examples/with-docker* images or Compose files (grep for 'with-docker' outside examples/ and docs/ found 0 hits); standalone output is tested without a container engine (e.g. test/e2e/app-dir/app/standalone.test.ts; 26 test files contain output: 'standalone') and graceful shutdown by test/production/graceful-shutdown/index.test.ts. No macOS or WSL test job.
code.dependencies: Manifests and direct counts: package.json (root, private workspace) 0 dependencies, 193 devDependencies, 12 pnpm patchedDependencies; packages/next/package.json 6 dependencies (@next/env, @swc/helpers, baseline-browser-mapping, caniuse-lite, postcss, styled-jsx), 6 peerDependencies (react, react-dom, @opentelemetry/api, @playwright/test, babel-plugin-react-compiler, sass; the last four optional), 1 optionalDependency (sharp ^0.35.4; platform @next/swc-* added at publish), 225 devDependencies (vendored into dist/compiled via ncc); packages/create-next-app/package.json 0 dependencies, 18 devDependencies (ncc-bundled); packages/next-swc/package.json 3 devDependencies; 19 package.json under packages/*; ~224 examples each with its own package.json. Cargo.toml (workspace): 166 [workspace.dependencies] entries (50 in-repo path crates + 116 external), 4 [patch.crates-io] git patches (bincode, virtue, mdxjs, include_dir) and a git dependency on triomphe (Cargo.toml:157-377). Lockfiles: pnpm-lock.yaml, Cargo.lock. pnpm-workspace.yaml:37-38 sets blockExoticSubdeps and minimumReleaseAge 2880 min (48 h). Engines: Node >=20.9.0 (packages/next/package.json:374-376), pnpm 10.33.0 (package.json:308), Rust nightly-2026-07-29 (rust-toolchain.toml:4; source builds only).
code.security_policy: none - no SECURITY.md anywhere in the tree (glob **/SECURITY.md and .github/SECURITY* empty). The only policy text is README.md:45-49: report privately by email to responsible.disclosure@vercel.com (bug-bounty programme); no SLA, supported-versions table or in-repo advisory process.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:19 - Rust-based JavaScript tooling 'for the fastest builds'
claim_checks.evidence: Rust tooling is real: Cargo workspace (Cargo.toml:4-18) with crates/next-napi-bindings, next-core, next-api and ~53 turbopack/crates, loaded as a native N-API addon by packages/next/src/build/swc/index.ts:202-306; Turbopack is the default bundler (docs/01-app/01-getting-started/01-installation.mdx:151-156). 'Fastest' is a superlative with no comparative measurement in the repo; the only numbers are project-reported compiler claims (docs/03-architecture/nextjs-compiler.mdx:8,19,245).

claim_checks.claim: docs 17-deploying.mdx:6 - deployable as Node.js server, Docker container, static export, or via adapters
claim_checks.evidence: Node server: `next start` -> startServer (packages/next/src/cli/next-start.ts:12,84). 'Docker' means standalone output: output:'standalone' emits .next/standalone with a generated server.js (packages/next/src/build/utils.ts:1418-1467; docs .../output.mdx:22-48), exercised without any container engine (26 test files contain output: 'standalone', e.g. test/e2e/app-dir/app/standalone.test.ts). Static export: output 'export' (server/config-shared.ts:1870-1878). Adapters: adapterPath hook (build/index.ts:4461-4481). No Docker-specific code besides is-docker detection (cli/next-info.ts:286-291; server/cache-dir.ts:2-10; telemetry/storage.ts:41-49), and no workflow or test builds the examples/with-docker* images.

claim_checks.claim: docs 17-deploying.mdx:44 - 'Docker deployments support all Next.js features'
claim_checks.evidence: The standalone server.js and `next start` both call the same startServer (build/utils.ts:1446-1467; cli/next-start.ts:84), so feature parity is by construction, but nothing in the repo runs the suite inside a container image. The docs qualify multi-instance use themselves: per-instance cache (self-hosting.mdx:89,109), per-build encryption key (:193-203), revalidateTag not propagated across instances (:273-275) - all needing cacheHandler/cacheHandlers or env configuration.

claim_checks.claim: examples/with-docker-compose/README.md:9 - Compose lets you 'Run multiple Next.js apps, databases, and other microservices in a single deployment'
claim_checks.evidence: True of Docker Compose generally, but the shipped compose files define exactly one service (next-app) with only a comment placeholder '# Add more containers below (nginx, postgres, etc.)' (compose.dev.yaml:1-31, compose.prod.yaml:1-22), no named volumes (dev only bind-mounts src/ and public/, compose.dev.yaml:16-18) and an external pre-created network (compose.dev.yaml:29-31). with-docker, with-docker-multi-env and with-docker-export-output likewise define Next.js services only (examples/with-docker/compose.yml:1-28; docker/production/compose.yaml:1-8; with-docker-export-output/compose.yml:1-27).

claim_checks.claim: docs output.mdx:54 - standalone server.js honours PORT and HOSTNAME env vars
claim_checks.evidence: packages/next/src/build/utils.ts:1437-1440 emits `parseInt(process.env.PORT, 10) || 3000`, `process.env.HOSTNAME || '0.0.0.0'` and KEEP_ALIVE_TIMEOUT (the last is not mentioned in output.mdx). Only some example Dockerfiles set HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0 (examples/with-docker/Dockerfile:82; with-docker-multi-env/docker/production/Dockerfile:54); the compose example's prod.Dockerfile:75 does not.

claim_checks.claim: docs self-hosting.mdx:299 - SIGINT/SIGTERM trigger graceful shutdown that finishes in-flight requests and pending after() callbacks
claim_checks.evidence: packages/next/src/server/lib/start-server.ts:399-480: server.close() waits for pending requests, then nextServer.close() and cleanup run, exiting 130 (SIGINT) / 143 (SIGTERM); the handlers are skipped when NEXT_MANUAL_SIG_HANDLE is set (:477-480); comment at :475 cites Docker. Covered by test/production/graceful-shutdown/index.test.ts. No drain timeout is implemented in this function (platform must provide one, as the docs say).

claim_checks.claim: docs self-hosting.mdx:89,109 - default cache is in-memory (50 MB) plus local disk, per instance
claim_checks.evidence: cacheMaxMemorySize default 50 * 1024 * 1024 (packages/next/src/server/config-shared.ts:2072); FileSystemCache uses an in-memory LRU when maxMemoryCacheSize is set and persists to the dist dir (packages/next/src/server/lib/incremental-cache/file-system-cache.ts:50-69); custom handler hook in server/lib/incremental-cache/index.ts:154,271.

claim_checks.claim: docs self-hosting.mdx:193-203 - NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY must be shared across instances; key is a base64 AES key embedded in build output
claim_checks.evidence: Runtime reads process.env.NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY first, else the manifest key, and imports it as AES-GCM after atob() (packages/next/src/server/app-render/encryption-utils.ts:74-88); when unset a 256-bit AES-GCM key is generated per build (encryption-utils-server.ts:97-129). Extra detail: when is-docker detects a container, no key cache is written between builds (encryption-utils-server.ts:44-50; server/cache-dir.ts:4-10).

claim_checks.claim: docs next.mdx:163 / CLI - telemetry is 'completely anonymous' and optional
claim_checks.evidence: Opt-out exists (`next telemetry disable`, NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED; packages/next/src/telemetry/storage.ts:135-154, cli/next-telemetry.ts:14-31) and no events are sent when disabled (storage.ts:312-315). 'Anonymous' is pseudonymous in practice: a persistent random anonymousId, a salted SHA-256 of the git remote URL (or cwd), CPU model, memory, OS release and Docker/WSL/CI/AI-agent flags are sent (anonymous-meta.ts:8-23; project-id.ts:43-47; post-telemetry-payload.ts:25). Any non-empty NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED value, including '0', disables it.

claim_checks.claim: docs ai-agents.mdx:63 / mcp.mdx:79-88,172 - `next dev` auto-generates AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md when an AI agent is detected; Next.js 16+ has a built-in /_next/mcp endpoint with 8 listed tools
claim_checks.evidence: Auto-generation confirmed: ensureAgentRulesForDev (packages/next/src/server/lib/app-info-log.ts:129-136), writeAgentFiles (generate-agent-files.ts:90-123), gated on agentRules !== false (start-server.ts:511-534), test test/development/app-dir/agent-rules-auto-generate/. MCP endpoint confirmed (server/mcp/get-mcp-middleware.ts:18; default on, config-shared.ts:2250). Docs tool list is out of date: code also registers get_request_insights (server/mcp/get-or-create-mcp-server.ts:67), and get_compilation_issues/compile_route are Turbopack-only (hot-reloader-webpack.ts:1698).

risks: Scope: nothing in this repo defines or runs multi-service container applications. Container material is docs plus four examples (with-docker, with-docker-compose, with-docker-multi-env, with-docker-export-output) that rely on the external Docker/Compose CLIs; product code only detects Docker (packages/next/src/cli/next-info.ts:286-291; server/cache-dir.ts:2-10; telemetry/storage.ts:41-49). The compose files define a single Next.js service each, with a placeholder comment for 'nginx, postgres, etc.' and no named volumes (examples/with-docker-compose/compose.dev.yaml:1-31, compose.prod.yaml:16); both with-docker services bind host port 3000 (examples/with-docker/compose.yml:12-13,26-27). No CI job or test builds or runs these examples (grep for 'with-docker' outside examples/ and docs/: 0 hits).

Example reproducibility: next is pinned to 'latest' (examples/with-docker/package.json:9; examples/with-docker-compose/next-app/package.json:9) with caret ranges for react/typescript, and the compose README warns build errors are more likely without a lockfile (examples/with-docker-compose/README.md:31-33); the compose example needs a manually created external network (compose.dev.yaml:29-31; README:44-46) and a fixed container_name (compose.dev.yaml:3); base images are tag-pinned only (node:20-alpine in prod.Dockerfile:3; node:24.13.0-slim in with-docker/Dockerfile:8) and READMEs ask users to bump them by hand (examples/with-docker/README.md:156-157); only some Dockerfiles set HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0 although the standalone server reads process.env.HOSTNAME (build/utils.ts:1438 vs compose example prod.Dockerfile:75).

Dev server in a container: docs advise against Docker for development on Mac/Windows because host-to-VM file sharing delays Fast Refresh (docs/01-app/02-guides/local-development.mdx:53-69). `next dev` binds all interfaces unless -H is given (bin/next.ts:342-345; server/lib/start-server.ts:309,554), moves to another port when the port is the default (cli/next-dev.ts:272; start-server.ts:300-309), blocks cross-origin dev-resource requests unless allowedDevOrigins lists them (server/lib/router-utils/block-cross-site-dev.ts:115-174), and serves an unauthenticated MCP endpoint at /_next/mcp that is on by default (config-shared.ts:2250; server/mcp/get-mcp-middleware.ts:11-46); requests without an Origin header are not blocked (block-cross-site-dev.ts:168-173).

Network and telemetry: telemetry is on by default and sends machine metadata plus a salted hash of the git remote to telemetry.nextjs.org from next build/dev (storage.ts:135-154; anonymous-meta.ts:8-23; post-telemetry-payload.ts:25); example Dockerfiles leave the disable line commented out (examples/with-docker/Dockerfile:49-52,84-87), so container builds report unless NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED is set. next/font/google needs fonts.googleapis.com at build time (packages/font/src/google/get-google-fonts-url.ts:50); a lockfile lacking the platform binary triggers a runtime download from the npm registry or a wasm fallback (build/swc/index.ts:262-293,308-383; lib/download-swc.ts:37-41); `next dev` queries registry.npmjs.org (hot-reloader-shared-utils.ts:17); create-next-app update-check has no opt-out found (create-next-app/index.ts:778-780).

State is container-local by default: cache is per-instance memory (50 MB, config-shared.ts:2072) plus disk (incremental-cache/file-system-cache.ts:50-69); revalidateTag does not propagate across instances without a custom handler (docs self-hosting.mdx:273-275); the Server Actions encryption key differs per build unless NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY is set, and inside Docker it is not cached between builds (encryption-utils-server.ts:44-50; cache-dir.ts:4-10); `.next` must be writable by the runtime user for prerender cache and optimized images (examples/with-docker/Dockerfile:92-94; README:134); NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are inlined at build time (self-hosting.mdx:39), so images are per-environment unless values are read at request time.

Workspace side effects: `next dev` creates or rewrites AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in the project root when it detects an AI coding agent, unless `agentRules: false` (packages/next/src/server/lib/start-server.ts:511-534; generate-agent-files.ts:90-123; docs ai-agents.mdx:63,85); create-next-app also generates them by default (docs installation.mdx:42). Agent detection uses env-var and filesystem probes (telemetry/agent-name.ts:5-25).

Artifact integrity is not verifiable from source: root .npmrc:4 sets provenance=true and the publish job has id-token: write (build_and_deploy.yml:629-631), but scripts/publish-release.js passes no --provenance flag and the workflow produces no checksums, signatures or release assets for the native .node binaries (build_and_deploy.yml:483-487 uploads workflow artifacts only). Installing `next` pulls optional per-platform native packages plus optional sharp (publish-release.js:208-217; packages/next/package.json:132-134), and CI installs wasm-pack through unpinned `curl ... | sh` (build_and_deploy.yml:535).

Platform, maintenance and policy: requires Node >=20.9.0 (packages/next/package.json:374-376); tests run on Linux ARM runners and Windows with no macOS or WSL test job (build_and_test.yml:443,940-1021; 'macos' only at build_and_deploy.yml:37,219 and build_reusable.yml:308-309); docs note glibc Linux Image Optimization may need allocator configuration (self-hosting.mdx:25); source builds need a pinned Rust nightly (rust-toolchain.toml:4) and git-patched crates (Cargo.toml:371-377); no SECURITY.md, only the README email (README.md:45-49).
